Posted March 16, 2006
See
 Steve Tuck Is A Free Man. Vindicated. Recuperating from Five Year Ordeal. Will Return to Mining Business in Canada After First Of Year.

MEDICAL MARIJUANA ADVOCATES LIFE TO BE MADE INTO A MOVIE
For Immediate Release
March 16, 2006
For more info contact: sisbroandco@rogers.com

Sisbro & Co. Inc., a small Canadian Film Production Company, has announced that it has acquired the rights to the life story of Steven Tuck who both Canadians and Americans alike came to know Tuck while he fought for refugee protection in Canada. 

In the fall of 2005, after Canada rejected his applications for refugee status, he was removed from an IV and taken from a Vancouver ER in handcuffs (with a catheter still attached) and forcibly turned over to US authorities to face marijuana cultivation charges in California. Just as he had predicted, he suffered incredible pain, when just as he had predicted he was held for a week without any medications, even antibiotics. The case received international publicity until he was released and taken to a hospital in Seattle.

This ordeal seriously damaged his health, but then, again exactly as he predicted, all charges for growing medical marijuana were dismissed! He has now largely recovered from that ordeal, and is now seeking readmission to Canada to pursue mining interests he developed while he was seeking refugee protection.

This biography will make an outstanding motion picture, says Kristen Soehner, Sisbro Producer.  It is definitely one of those stories that proves that truth is stranger than fiction.

Written by Sisbro Screenwriter and Director James Henderson, the tale begins with Steve Tuck's wild and unpredictable life in Kentucky.  A stint in the military left him a paraplegic after a parachuting accident on a classified mission in Central America.

He's had over thirteen operations on his spine, says Henderson.  He had to learn to walk again.  Cannabis is the only drug that keeps the pain at bay and the only reason he has been able to prolong his life.  His story is not just about cannabis it's about courage, intelligence, and compassion. *

Consequently, Tuck has spent his adult life attempting to convince governments to legalize medical marijuana.  Some of the people with whom he has worked have remarkable and heart-wrenching stories themselves, adds Henderson.

It has been a difficult script to write, because there is so much to tell. In one ironic twist, Tuck found himself battling organized crime when they started growing marijuana on a mining claim he was exploring in British Columbia. Of course, the police tried to arrest him instead of the gangsters who were shooting at him.

Although we do want to present a film that will foster debate, it's also about brave human beings who have had to fight the very people who should have been helping them.

Soehner says that several outstanding actors are considering roles in the film.  Of course, we are still working on the funding, the bane of all producers existences, she says, laughing.  But we believe that it will happen there are many people out there who not only support Steve's cause but who would just love to see a great film made about a man who is dynamic, fascinating and depending upon your view, a true hero or anti-hero.*

Sisbro's producers and director can be contacted at sisbroandco@rogers.com for further information.
